name: National Fuel Niagara Expansion Phase I
monitor_reason: length: no new National Fuel pipe; compression and pressure uprate only
researcher_notes: A Federal Register notice from October 3, 1996 describes the 1997 Niagara Expansion. National Fuel's part, under docket CP96-671, was compression and pressure work only. It added horsepower at the Concord station in New York, replaced compressor units at the Ellisburg station in Pennsylvania, and raised the maximum operating pressure on Line X-North and Line XM-2 from 720 to 780 psig. It moved up to 48,000 dekatherms per day. No new pipe is listed for National Fuel. The pipe loops in that notice (10.6, 6.7 and 5.5 miles) belong to Transco under docket CP96-545, so they are not National Fuel pipe. The EIA August 2026 release, Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 49, lists NFGS Niagara Expansion Phase I as New Pipeline with 139 miles and docket CP96-545. That docket belongs to Transco, so the EIA row appears to mix two projects and the 139 miles has no support. The project is completed (1997), so it fails the 25 km new-pipe rule and the sponsor and endpoints are not in doubt. No new row. Not a match to an existing row: existing National Fuel rows P2537, P6878 and P7827 are different projects.
